extracted.intended_audience: readers of scientific reviews and specialists interested in evolutionary theory (Victorian/academic readership)
extracted.subtask_description: A published counter-criticism arguing about the roles of natural selection, heredity, variation, and use/disuse in organic evolution; aimed at rebutting another author's claims and clarifying causal attribution in evolutionary change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three essential factors of natural selection
rubrics_metrics.description: "The process has three factors — heredity, variation, and external action — any one of which being absent, the process ceases."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three corresponing ideas are co-essential; none alone is the 'central idea' of natural selection. When evaluating claims about natural selection, check that variation, heredity, and differential external action (e.g., mortality or differential reproduction) are all present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of differential advantage for natural selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural variations can be maintained and increased by natural selection only if the individuals bearing them derive advantages in the struggle for existence "sufficiently great to aid their survival and multiplication in considerable degrees."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To attribute a trait's origin to natural selection, demonstrate that the trait confers a meaningful reproductive or survival advantage that affects family/lineage multiplication over generations; small or neutral changes are unlikely to be fixed by selection alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use/disuse (functionally-produced) modifications may operate independently of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: If acquired (functionally-produced) structural changes are inherited, they can cause species-wide change without the supplanting of some stocks by others, and thus may accumulate independently of natural selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating causes of morphological change, consider whether the change affects members of a population broadly (e.g., due to shared environment or habit) such that inheritance of acquired modifications could explain the change without invoking differential survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural selection does not 'cover' all causes operating through inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The statement that natural selection includes and covers all the causes which can possibly operate through inheritance is quite erroneous."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume every inherited change must have been produced or maintained by natural selection; consider alternative hereditary mechanisms (e.g., inheritance of functionally-induced changes or persistent fortuitous variations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for using domesticated/bred examples as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances from domestic breeding (greyhounds, pointers, setters) are not automatically valid evidence for inheritance-by-use because their characters may be due primarily to artificial selection or breeder choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether observed breed traits arise from habitual use/disuse or from artificial selection practices; account for breeder-driven selection of puppies and other confounding factors before inferring use/disuse inheritance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent inheritance of fortuitous structural variations without selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Fortuitous structural variations (e.g., polydactyly — 'one of those persons... who has an additional finger') can be transmitted for generations even when they confer no advantage or disadvantage, and natural selection "never comes into play at all."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a trait is heritable but neutral with respect to fitness, its persistence should not be taken as evidence of natural selection; consider genetic transmission and admixture as explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria distinguishing when natural selection co-operates with use-induced inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural selection will co-operate with inheritance of functionally-produced changes when those changes also confer differential fitness (e.g., migration into presence of faster prey: muscular strengthening aids survival and is then favored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for cases where functionally-induced variation both spreads through inheritance and also differentially increases reproductive success; only then can selection amplify the inherited functional changes over generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current scientific status: inheritance of acquired characters is disputed
rubrics_metrics.description: Biologists (at the time of writing) dispute the inheritance of organs enfeebled by disuse and also dispute inheritance of increases caused by use; the matter is not 'not generally disputed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat claims of inheritance of acquired characters as contested; require robust empirical evidence (referenced discussions, meetings, or experiments) before accepting such inheritance as established.
